title: Global dataset on heat wave exposure due to the urban heat island effect
abstract: Continuing global warming and urbanization have increased the frequency and severity of extreme heat events in cities. Therefore, understanding how the urban heat island (UHI) effect influences cities is essential for developing effective mitigation and prevention strategies. A 1-km resolution dataset was constructed to assess heat-wave exposure attributable to UHIs in urban human settlements worldwide from 2003 to 2020. An adaptive urban-rural threshold method was employed to delineate the spatial extent of UHI impacts, and a spatiotemporally fitted MODIS surface temperature dataset was used to address missing data caused by cloud contamination. This dataset explicitly separates the contributions of background climate, local landscape characteristics, and urbanization to heat wave exposure, providing a scientific basis for identifying key UHI mitigation areas and developing heat wave risk early warning models that account for UHI effects. The proposed methodology and dataset support synergistic decision-making for integrating urban climate adaptation with sustainable development, and the technical framework can be extended to studies of UHIs and heat wave exposure in other regions worldwide.
problem: Few studies have successfully disentangled the specific contribution of the urban heat island effect from background climate and local landscape characteristics when assessing heat wave exposure, hindering the development of targeted mitigation strategies for cities.
method: This study proposes a method using a spatiotemporally fitted temperature dataset and an adaptive urban-rural threshold to quantify global heat wave exposure, explicitly separating the additional exposure in person-days attributable to the urban heat island effect from the background climate.
task: The task is to construct a global dataset assessing urban heat wave exposure from 2003 to 2020, specifically quantifying the additional exposure caused by the urban heat island (UHI) effect.

kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: The temperature data used in this study were obtained from the MODIS Gap-Filled Long-Term Land Surface Temperature Daily dataset. According to the data provider, cross-validation against raw MODIS observations indicates that the root mean square errors of the gap-filled data at midday (1:30 p.m.) and midnight (1:30 a.m.) LSTs are 1.88 K and 1.33 K, respectively.

dynamics of UHI-related heat wave exposure. Figure 4 shows the changes in UHI-induced heat-wave exposure across different regions worldwide. For example, in the East Asia-Pacific (EAP) region, the heat wave exposure caused by UHI is significantly higher than in other regions. Compared with 2005, total heat wave exposure caused by UHI in 2020 has increased in the Europe and Central Asia (ECA), Latin America (LAC), Middle East and North Africa (MENA), North America (NA), and Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) regions, whereas it decreased in the South Asia (SAR) region. Interpretation of these patterns provides valuable insights for heat wave prevention and mitigation at both global and regional scales.
